I'm computing the N-CA-CB-CG dihedral angle for this ASP residue, taking cross products of the bond vectors to find the normal vectors needed for the torsion calculation.

Computing n1×n2 and dotting with b2 gives a positive value, so the dihedral angle comes out to +60° using atan2 with the sign convention.

I'm double-checking this with an alternative projection method, decomposing b1 into components perpendicular to the normalized b2 vector to verify the +60° (gauche+) result rather than the more typical -60° or 180° seen for Asp chi1.

Computing the angle between these two perpendicular vectors, I get a cosine of roughly -0.5, suggesting an angle near 120°, which seems off and worth double-checking.

I'm second-guessing the sign convention for dihedral angles — the correct formula involves projections using the vector from p2 to p1 (reversed b1) and from p3 to p4 (b3), so I need to revisit which vectors I'm actually comparing.

Dotting the cross product with u gives a positive value, confirming the rotation is +60°, so this is a g+ rotamer. That's plausible for Asp, occurring occasionally, so I'll go with it.
